correctness.rationale: For a nondegenerate positive rate mixing law with finite third moment, A,B,C,E and their derivatives are defined. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz gives B²<AC and C²<BE, hence Q=A-B²/C is positive and strictly decreasing. The exact derivative hU′=C(A(U)-Q)/(A-A(U))² proves the iff cutoff and exactly one interior minimum; equality at the left boundary is handled. Implicit differentiation verifies increasing trough location and the linear critical onset. For finite rate mixtures the two-smallest-rate expansion of Q gives the stated large-U law. A standalone standard-library program verified 3,000 random rate mixtures on both cutoff sides, 6,000 finite differences, the two-rate exact threshold and finite-support asymptotics. These finite computations are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2014 seismology paper explicitly gives untruncated rate-mixture slopes and simulates magnitude-cutoff upturns, so these are excluded from the claimed contribution. Its accessible author-uploaded article text, including formulas (1),(2),(6), cutoff simulations (Fig. 2) and conclusions, does not give the iff normalized-rate-variance cutoff, a strict all-mixing-law single-trough theorem, or the finite-mixture two-slowest-rate asymptotic. Broader hazard-mixture papers located describe mixing increasing-hazard components, not specifically right-conditioning an arbitrary exponential-rate mixture. Statement-based comparisons with indexed published mathematical results did not identify an implication equivalent to the combined claim. Full-text limitations and the possibility of unstated general truncation theorems are explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: General reliability-theory work may contain an implicit version of the sharp cutoff criterion; a complete bibliographic survey was not possible.
Full text of Navarro et al. (2009) and Block et al. (2008) was not inspected, so an unexpectedly broad general theorem cannot be excluded.
The 2014 source’s finite-cutoff simulation behavior is prior art; only the stated exact universal classification and two-slowest asymptotic are claimed.
Finite-sample b-value estimation and catalog truncation are distinct from the differential slope and conditioning considered here.

value.rationale: The 2014 seismology literature motivates an actual ambiguity between heterogeneous magnitudes and finite upper cutoffs, but lacks a universal criterion for when a local logarithmic-slope trough can exist. This finding gives a necessary-and-sufficient rate-heterogeneity threshold for every positive mixing law with finite third moment, proves the full turning-point topology, and identifies a two-slowest-rate control of the trough’s large-cutoff position. These have clear mathematical roles in magnitude-distribution interpretation and are not simply a chosen numeric example, code check or a renamed known untruncated mixture property. Applicability to finite fitted catalogs is expressly limited.
